L1Variant.description:
One candidate variant proposed by ``l1_generate``.

Three override slots, each carrying a different layer's mutations:

- ``pipeline_params_override`` — per-node tunables, shape ``{node:
  {param: value}}``. Inner shape is grafted at runtime by
  :func:`l1_validators.build_l1_output_schema` from the active
  ``PipelineSchema``; the keys at this level remain ``dict[str, dict]``
  so the Pydantic parse never fails on a legitimately backend-specific
  node name.
- ``prompt_fields_override`` — top-level prompt fields, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``PROMPT_STRING_FIELDS``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.
- ``task_context_override`` — pipeline-context strings, shape
  ``{field_name: string}``. Keys constrained to ``TASK_CONTEXT_OVERRIDES``
  by the runtime-built JSON Schema.

At least one of the three must be non-empty — an all-empty variant is
a no-op and is rejected by :func:`detect_invariants` downstream with
``reason="no_op_variant"``.

``target_axis`` and ``reasoning`` are LLM-side reasoning aids — the
``l1_generate`` prompt's ``answer_format`` instructs the model to
emit them so its candidate selection is grounded. PromptPotter
persists them in the audit trail but doesn't read them at runtime;
they're recorded so a human reviewing ``round_NNNN.json`` can see
the model's stated rationale for each candidate.

pipeline_params_override.description: Per-node tunables, shape {node_name: {param: value}}. Inner per-node properties are grafted from the active PipelineSchema at runtime.
pipeline_params_override.title: Pipeline Params Override

prompt_fields_override.title: Prompt Fields Override

task_context_override.description: Pipeline-context strings; keys must be one of {upstream_context, downstream_context}.
task_context_override.title: Task Context Override

L1Variant.title: L1Variant

VariantEvidenceGrounding.description:
One row of evidence justifying a variant's chosen mutation.

``field`` names the panel entry the LLM is grounding on. The JSON
Schema exported to the provider lists the allowed values as an
``enum`` hint so structured-output-aware models stay in-set, but the
parse boundary is permissive — providers like Groq don't honor the
enum and a single off-script value would otherwise crash the round.
The canonical enforcement is the ``evidence_grounding_present``
behavior check (see :mod:`l1_behavior`); ``stall_exploration`` is the
escape hatch and is only valid when
``escalation_panel.exploration_budget`` is ``normal`` or ``wide``.

field.description: One of EVIDENCE_GROUNDING_FIELDS — panel entry cited.
field.title: Field

Critique returned at round-end. Three load-bearing fields only:
``priority_fix`` (the headline steer), ``failure_highlights`` (per-

Prose ``summary`` + ``positive_critique`` + ``negative_critique``

other open clusters.

L1SituationalExample.description:
One worked example pinned to an active trigger.

Renders in L1's prompt only when ``trigger_id`` matches either an
auto-trigger that fired this round (PEAKED axis, runtime_failure,
chain_bind, continuous_envelope, latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity)
or the ``rule_id`` of a currently-authored
:class:`L1SupplementalRule`. Empty trigger ⇒ silent.
L1SituationalExample.title: L1SituationalExample

L1SupplementalRule.description:
One situational rule appended to L1's instruction next round.

Authored by L2 when the panels show a recurring L1 failure mode that
L1's static instruction does not address and the dispatch hub's
auto-trigger registry (`dispatch/hub/auto_rules.py::AUTO_RULES`)
does not already cover. Renders inline via the
``l1_supplemental_rules`` dispatch-hub injection — the rule body
appears in L1's prompt prefixed with its ``rule_id`` and tagged with
the citation L2 used to motivate it.
L1SupplementalRule.title: L1SupplementalRule

schema.description:
L2 refinement. All fields optional — the LLM sets only what it
wants to change.

``task_context`` is a free-form refinement dict (keys: domain,
pipeline_purpose, data_characteristics, optimization_goals,
key_challenges) — left as ``dict[str, Any]`` because the cycle's
:class:`TaskDecomposition` owns the precise key set and merges via
:meth:`TaskDecomposition.merge`. ``l1_layout`` is a similarly
flexible ``{slot: [placeholder, ...]}`` map validated downstream by
:func:`validate_l1_layout`.

``l1_supplemental_rules`` + ``l1_situational_examples`` are
full-replace layers that L2 re-authors every fire. Auto-triggered
rules (PEAKED, runtime_failure, chain_bind, continuous_envelope,
latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity) render independently via the
dispatch hub's auto-rules registry — L2 only adds rules that
auto-triggers don't already cover.
schema.title: L2ContextOutput

ForkProposal.description:
L3-emitted proposal to rewind the search to an earlier round.

Observation-only in v1: recorded to ``round_NNNN.json`` so the
operator can read it and manually fork via
``python -m promptpotter resume --from N`` or
``--fork-on-divergence`` if the proposal looks sound. No automatic
fork is triggered — this is the *selection* signal half of the
M13+ AlphaZero-shaped-MCTS arc, shipped without the backprop /
UCB-selection-rule halves. See
``docs/research/related-work.md#comparison-to-mcts``.
ForkProposal.title: ForkProposal

l1_generate/1.persona: You are a pipeline optimization expert.
l1_generate/1.task_intent: Generate {{n_variants}} candidate configurations that improve on the parent searchpoint. The target pipeline, its domain, last round's critique, and the failures so far are described in the context blocks below — do not assume any specific task type. The critique block names the priority fix and suggested axes from L1_CRITIQUE; treat it as the primary steer for what to mutate this round.
l1_generate/1.instruction:
Produce up to {{n_variants}} candidates — return fewer rather than padding with clones. Never mix axes in one candidate — each candidate changes exactly one axis.

INVALID-prevention (hard reject — burn these in your head before you write any candidate): observed across rounds 4–5 of the active AIME campaign, L1_GENERATE repeatedly proposes pipeline-param values that the validator rejects, wasting the slot. The most common offenders are `llm_only.reasoning_effort ∈ {medium, high}` (only `low` is permitted on this dataset) and `llm_only.model ∈ {openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini, openai/gpt-oss-20b:nitro, openai/gpt-oss-20b}` (only the campaign-configured model is permitted; the catalogue lists the exact allowed set). Before emitting any candidate touching a param axis, confirm the value appears in `pipeline_param_catalogue.allowed_values` for that param — if it does not, drop the candidate entirely and use the slot for a prompt-field mutation. Re-proposing a value the runtime_failures panel already lists is the single largest wasted-budget pattern in the archive; the validator will reject the variant before any backend call, so the budget is gone with zero signal returned.

- Scalar axis: change a single param value.
- Prompt axis: coherent rewrite of 2–3 subfields from {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style}.
- Structured-output axis: 2–3-edit rewrite of answer_format. Preserve LaTeX and escape sequences character-for-character — corrupted backslashes (e.g. '\boxed' becoming 'oxed') waste the slot.
- Field semantics: prompt-field values (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format) are literal strings concatenated verbatim with the sample's query at wire-time — the backend injects the query, the field value MUST NOT reference the input via any placeholder slot. Any value containing a fill-in-the-blank pattern is rejected as a template (not a prompt) and counts as wasted budget. Forbidden patterns include but are not limited to: bracketed slots (`[insert X]`, `[your X]`, `[example]`, `[N]`, `[problem]`), brace-templated slots (single-brace `{x}`, `{problem}` or double-brace equivalents), and angle-bracketed slots (`<x>`, `<query>`). The rule is the shape, not the wordlist: anything that looks like a hole the writer expects to be filled later belongs in a template engine, not in a prompt field.

Across the {{n_variants}}, every candidate must touch a different axis — duplicates are rejected. Stronger requirement: the batch MUST cover ≥4 DISTINCT prompt-field axes from {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format}. A batch concentrating all proposals on one axis (e.g. 5/6 variants all mutating `instruction`) is rejected as a search-monoculture even when the wordings differ — single-axis search saturates at the 60% plateau the AIME archive has been stuck at. The 60%-tier winners on this dataset landed on three different prompt-field axes (instruction in `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_80d0254d/R1`, answer_format in `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_7cb613c4/R4`, problem_description in `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_aa70ee77/R5`), and reaching 60%+ requires unioning hits across axes — so cover the space. Empty variants are rejected: each variant MUST mutate at least one field across the three override slots (pipeline_params_override, prompt_fields_override, task_context_override). A mutation that is a substring, truncation, lowercase variant, or paraphrase of the parent's value on the chosen field is a clone, not a mutation. Prompt rewrites must introduce concepts, constraints, or framing NOT already in the parent's value on the chosen field — 'focus on X, Y, Z' where X/Y/Z are already named in the parent is restatement, and vague nudges like 'add more context' or 'clarify the task' dilute focus. Param-field axes are LAST RESORT. Of your {{n_variants}} candidates, AT MOST 1 may target a PARAM-FIELD axis (temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort, top_p) — and that one is only allowed when L1_CRITIQUE.suggested_axes explicitly names a param axis or runtime_failures contains a quantitative signature (empty response, HTTP 413, latency timeout). The remaining variants MUST target PROMPT-FIELD axes (persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style). `answer_format` is reserved for genuine format errors only — do not mutate it for reasoning improvements. This bias exists because prompt-field axes carry the real lift; param axes typically peak in the first 1-2 rounds and further mutations on them waste budget. For each, the reasoning field MUST cite a specific item from the critique block (priority_fix, a suggested_axis, or a failure_highlight) — variants that ignore the critique are wasted budget.

Consult runtime_failures before proposing. Configs already listed there (matching axis + value, e.g. `max_tokens=2048` on a problem that recorded `llm_only:empty_response`, or any combination that recorded `HTTP 413`) failed for a measured reason — do not re-propose them. To revisit that region of the search space, change a different axis at the same time so the new variant is not a repeat.

Continuous-axis envelope: for numeric knobs (max_tokens, temperature, top_p), stay within ±50% of the parent value unless one of these justifies a larger jump — (a) a sibling_yield row on the axis with mean_delta > 0, (b) a runtime_failures entry pointing at the parent value, or (c) escalation_panel.exploration_budget = wide. Larger jumps without that grounding are speculation, not exploration.

Acting on task_context (chain-binding rule): when task_context names an L1 axis to target (look for the verbatim phrase `targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'`) and quotes a failure cluster from L1_CRITIQUE, AT LEAST one variant in your batch MUST target that named axis and use the quoted failure cluster (or a verbatim substring) as the evidence_grounding.citation with field=task_context. This closes the chain L1_SCORE → L1_CRITIQUE → L2_CONTEXT → L1_GENERATE so cross-round learning compounds. Skipping a task_context directive when one is present counts as wasted budget — the variant slot was meant to test what L2 just framed. If task_context has no `targeting L1 axis` directive (round 1 or L2 hasn't fired), proceed as usual — this rule activates only when L2 has explicitly named an axis.

Reading axis_memory (HARD RULE — read this before proposing any pipeline_params mutation): each entry in `axis rankings` is the FULL fact about that axis. A high `effect` number is NOT a green light to mutate. When the entry includes `PEAKED — do not mutate without sibling_yield>0 or exploration_budget=wide rebut`, the parent's current value IS the measured peak; mutating that axis is regression by default and the variant will be rejected by the evidence_grounding_present behaviour check. To override the peak, the reasoning field MUST quote one of: (a) a sibling_yield row on this axis with mean_delta>0 this round, or (b) escalation_panel.exploration_budget = wide. Both must be real entries from the panels — fabricated citations count as no rebut.

One-shot worked example — REJECTED rationale: `axis_rankings: llm_only.temperature (effect=0.245, consistently_impactful, PEAKED — do not mutate without sibling_yield>0 or exploration_budget=wide rebut)`. A variant with `target_axis: llm_only.temperature`, `pipeline_params_override: {llm_only: {temperature: 0.5}}`, `reasoning: "Axis memory shows temperature has the highest effect; lowering it should help."`, `evidence_grounding: {field: axis_memory, citation: "temperature effect=0.245"}` is REJECTED — it cites the effect number but ignores the PEAKED tag on the same line, and names no rebut. ACCEPTED rationale on the same axis_memory: `target_axis: persona`, mutating `prompt_fields_override.persona`, `evidence_grounding: {field: critique, citation: "priority_fix: 'sharpen verification mindset on combinatorial counting'"}` — different axis, anchored in critique, no peaked-axis conflict.

Underspecification rule: every variant MUST make its intended behaviour change concrete enough that a reader who has not seen this round's panels can tell what changed and why it would help. The combination of (target_axis, changes_description, reasoning, evidence_grounding.citation) MUST name (i) which observed failure pattern or panel signal the mutation addresses, (ii) what the candidate value/wording does differently from the parent, and (iii) the expected directional effect. Vague mutations ("improve reasoning", "adjust temperature", "better format") fail this contract.

Repair garbled tokens inherited from the parent prompt, plan, or critique before referencing them. LaTeX-corrupted strings (`oxed` for `\boxed`), truncated words (`athematical` for `mathematical`), or other artifacts must be fixed in your mutation, not propagated into changes_description or any prompt field.

Additive prompt-field rule (load-bearing) — prompt-field mutations on {persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style} are ADDITIVE. The parent field carries load-bearing scaffolding the current accuracy depends on: format anchors (`\boxed{N}`, JSON contracts, output-shape directives), role credentials (`AIME math expert`, `competition-math grader`), structural cues. Preserve those verbatim, then refine or extend around them. Replacing a prompt-field whole-cloth drops scaffolding and produces hard regressions — observed prior sweep on AIME 2025: a persona rewrite that dropped the parent's `\boxed{N}` directive scored 0.00 / 20, and a thinking_style rewrite that lost the parent's answer-anchoring scored 0.17 / 20, both regressing hard from a 0.50 origin. The rule: your new value for the chosen field MUST contain the literal substring of every output directive, format anchor, and proper-noun role token present in the parent's value on that same field. New content is appended or interpolated around them, never substituted for them. A mutation whose new value is disjoint from the parent's scaffolding fails the evidence_grounding_present behaviour check as a structural-regression clone-class.

One-shot additive example — Parent persona on this round: `You are an AIME math expert. Always use \boxed{N} for the final integer answer.` REJECTED mutation: `You are a competition-math specialist who double-checks combinatorial counting carefully.` — lost the `\boxed{N}` anchor and the parent role token; accuracy collapses to 0. ACCEPTED mutation: `You are an AIME math expert who double-checks each combinatorial-counting step and verifies parity before stating the final answer. Always use \boxed{N} for the final integer answer.` — preserves both the `AIME math expert` role token and the `\boxed{N}` anchor verbatim; adds the verification refinement around them.

Minimal-diff-additive rule (load-bearing) — when mutating a prompt-field on the named L1 axis from L1_CRITIQUE or task_context, prefer the SMALLEST POSSIBLE additive edit that injects ONE new failure-cluster keyword or trigger phrase. Single-clause appends and connective-pattern swaps ("verify X, Y, Z before proceeding" → "after every X, Y, Z, verify") have empirically out-performed full rewrites by ~10 accuracy points on AIME 2025. The pattern: identify the missing concept named in L1_CRITIQUE.failure_highlights or task_context.key_challenges (a verb, noun, or domain keyword the parent's field does not contain), and splice it into the parent's existing sentence structure with minimum surrounding edits. Whole-sentence rewrites that paraphrase the parent without injecting a new keyword are clones in this scheme — they fail the underspecification rule because no observed-failure-pattern keyword was added.

One-shot minimal-diff worked example (AIME 2025, real R1 winner from cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_80d0254d, lifted origin from 0.500 → 0.600 on a single-axis edit): Parent instruction: `Solve the problem step by step, explicitly verify each algebraic expansion, factorization, and simplification before proceeding.` L1_CRITIQUE priority_fix: `'emphasize step-by-step verification'`, failure_highlights cited combinatorial-counting misses on a 3×9 grid problem. WINNER mutation: `Solve the problem step by step, and after every algebraic expansion, factorization, or combinatorial count, explicitly verify the correctness before proceeding.` Two precise changes: (a) added the missing failure-cluster keyword `combinatorial count` (the parent only named algebraic ops, but the misses clustered around combinatorial counting), (b) swapped connective pattern `verify X, Y, Z before proceeding` → `after every X, Y, Z, verify ... before proceeding` (the trigger pattern makes verification a per-step gate, not a one-time review). Everything else preserved verbatim. REJECTED clone-class on the same axis: a full rewrite like `Carefully analyze the problem, identify the relevant mathematical structure, and methodically work through each step while validating intermediate results.` — it paraphrases the parent's intent without injecting any failure-cluster keyword from the critique; it is a vague nudge that fails the underspecification rule.

ROUND-1 RELIABILITY MODE — activates when the parent SearchPoint IS the origin (no prior round has been scored yet, no L1_CRITIQUE block is present in the panels, the cycle has zero accumulated runtime_failures from prior rounds). This is the first L1_GENERATE call of the campaign and its quality determines the campaign floor. The goal in this mode is RELIABILITY, not creative exploration: the round-winner should reach ≥60% accuracy with high probability, not 60% on a lucky lottery draw. Empirically, across 25+ AIME forks the unmodified template hit 60% on R1 in only 1 fork (`cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_80d0254d/R1`); every other fork plateaued lower or took until R4–R5 to reach the same number. To make R1 a reliable floor, the batch MUST include at least one variant from each of the three confirmed-winning patterns below; the remaining variants extend coverage onto unused prompt-field axes. Treat each pattern as a recipe — identify the parent-field equivalent in the current dataset's prompt, then apply the minimal-diff additive edit per the rules above.

PATTERN A — Instruction with per-step verification trigger (winning lineage: `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_80d0254d/R1`, lifted origin from 0.50 → 0.60 on a single-axis edit). Locate the parent's `instruction` field. Inject one missing failure-cluster keyword from a panel signal (or from the parent's pipeline_purpose if no critique yet), AND swap the verification connective from `verify X, Y, Z before proceeding` to `after every X, Y, Z, verify ... before proceeding` so the gate fires per-step rather than as a one-time review. Preserve every existing format anchor and role token verbatim.

PATTERN B — Answer-format with parsing scaffolding (winning lineage: `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_7cb613c4/R4`, 0.55 → 0.60). Locate the parent's `answer_format` field. Add explicit parsing scaffolding around the final answer — e.g. require the boxed answer be placed on its own line preceded by a literal `Answer:` marker, or restructure to a two-stage layout (a reasoning block, then a delimiter, then the boxed final answer). Preserve every existing format anchor (`\boxed{N}`, JSON contracts, etc.) verbatim per the additive rule.

PATTERN C — Problem-description with restatement directive (winning lineage: `cycle_926e2029d11a_fork_aa70ee77/R5`, 0.55 → 0.60). Locate the parent's `problem_description` field. Add a directive requiring the model to restate or paraphrase the input problem in its own words BEFORE beginning any calculation, ensuring correct interpretation of the question. This catches mis-read failures that recycled `verify each step` wording cannot. Preserve every existing role token and constraint statement verbatim.

The remaining {{n_variants}} − 3 variants in R1 MODE should extend coverage onto unused prompt-field axes — for example a `persona` with a domain-specialist role token (`AIME combinatorics medalist who decomposes by orbit-stabilizer`, `modular-arithmetic geometer who reaches for Chinese Remainder before brute force`), a `thinking_style` mandating multi-pass cross-checking (`solve via method A; then solve via a structurally different method B; if they disagree, present both and pick the one whose derivation has fewer arithmetic steps`), or a `task_intent` declaring a sharper success criterion. DO NOT mutate the same prompt-field axis more than twice across the R1 batch; the cover-the-axes requirement above is load-bearing in R1 because there is no prior critique to steer toward a specific failure cluster, so axis coverage IS the search strategy. Param-axis mutations are NOT eligible in R1 MODE — every R1 slot must target a prompt-field axis (the param-axis last-resort rule above is upgraded to a hard-no in R1 since no panel signal yet justifies a param mutation).
l1_generate/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with key "variants" containing an array of {{n_variants}} objects, each with:
  - "variant_name": short identifier
  - "changes_description": 1-2 sentence description
  - Three override slots — each holds a different layer's mutations; never conflate them. At least one slot MUST be non-empty (an all-empty variant is a no-op and is rejected).
    * "pipeline_params_override": per-node tunables, nested {node_name: {param: value}}, e.g. {"llm_only": {"temperature": 0.7}}. Used for backend tunables only — NOT prompt text, NOT pipeline-context fields. Do not put any of the prompt-field or task-context keys inside a node dict here.
    * "prompt_fields_override": top-level prompt-template fields as a flat {field: string} dict. Keys MUST be one of: persona, task_intent, problem_description, instruction, thinking_style, answer_format. Any other key is rejected by the schema.
    * "task_context_override": pipeline-context strings as a flat {field: string} dict. Keys MUST be one of: upstream_context, downstream_context. These inject pipeline awareness into the target prompt.
  - "target_axis": the primary parameter axis this candidate focuses on
  - "reasoning": why this combination is promising — must satisfy the underspecification rule (name the failure pattern, the concrete value/wording change, and the expected directional effect)
  - "evidence_grounding": object naming the panel field that justifies the mutation. `field` ∈ {parent_panel, sibling_yield, axis_memory, escalation_panel, task_context, plan, critique, stall_exploration}; `citation` is a short string quoting or naming the specific entry (e.g. `"sibling_yield: persona axis n_beat_parent=3/4 mean_delta=+0.08"` or `"task_context.optimization_goals: 'reduce verbosity'"`). The contract is: no data justifying a choice ⇒ do not gamble. `stall_exploration` is the explicit-stall escape hatch — only valid when `escalation_panel.exploration_budget` is `normal` or `wide`. When `field == "axis_memory"` and the cited axis is tagged PEAKED, the citation MUST also name the rebut (sibling_yield row or wide exploration) verbatim or the variant fails the evidence_grounding_present check.

l1_critique/1.persona: You are a pipeline evaluation analyst.
l1_critique/1.task_intent: Analyze the evaluation results below and produce a structured critique for the next optimization round.
l1_critique/1.instruction:
Read the measurements above. Extract the dominant failure cluster, name the L1 axis that targets it, and write the concrete change.

`priority_fix` MUST follow `<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>` where `<axis>` is a real pipeline axis (node param key or one of persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style/answer_format), `<concrete change>` is a specific edit ("add coordinate-verification step", not "improve reasoning"), and `<quoted failure pattern>` matches a cluster you name in `failure_highlights`.

`failure_highlights`: each entry quotes the failing sample's query stem (~80c verbatim), predicted answer (~80c), and ground truth. Prefix shared-root-cause entries with a cluster label, e.g. "Coordinate geometry (3/N): Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...". These are the ONLY per-sample failures L2 and the next L1 see — quote samples, don't summarize.

`suggested_axes`: ≤4 real pipeline axes for L2 to consider.
l1_critique/1.thinking_style: Reason from the measurements, not from priors about what usually helps. If the data is thin on an axis, say so rather than guessing.
l1_critique/1.answer_format:
Return JSON:
{
  "priority_fix": "<axis>: <concrete change> — addresses <quoted failure pattern>",
  "suggested_axes": ["<real pipeline axis>", ...],
  "failure_highlights": ["<cluster_label? Query: ... | Predicted: ... | GT: ...>", ...]
}
Caps: suggested_axes ≤ 4, failure_highlights ≤ 3 each ≤ 140c, priority_fix ≤ 200c.

l2_context/1.persona: You are L2: the framing layer. You refine `task_context` — the 5-field steering dict every layer (L1, L1_CRITIQUE, L2, L3) reads next round. You do not author candidate prompts.
l2_context/1.task_intent: Primary job: nudge `task_context` so L1's next round mutates a real failure cluster. Optional: add a supplemental rule, pin a worked example, restructure L1's layout. A no-op `task_context` (paraphrase only) is rejected as verbatim-repeat and escalates to L3.
l2_context/1.instruction:
PRIMARY: refine task_context. All 5 fields non-empty after fire. Nudge from one data point — paraphrase = no-op = L3 escalation.

  domain · pipeline_purpose · data_characteristics · optimization_goals — 1–2 sentences each, framing only.
  key_challenges — THE chain-bind: (a) failure cluster from critique, (b) the literal phrase `targeting L1 axis '<axis_name>'`, (c) concrete change. This phrase appears HERE ONLY.

Axis pick: SEMANTIC failure (wrong reasoning, missed case, refusal) → prompt-field axis (persona/task_intent/problem_description/instruction/thinking_style). QUANTITATIVE failure with runtime_failures signature → param axis.

Divergence: scan CURRENT PROMPT above. If your change is already there, switch axis or write STRICTER.

OPTIONAL (skip unless warranted):
  l1_supplemental_rules — ONLY for failure modes NOT in SITUATIONAL RULES above (auto-covered: peaked_axis, runtime_failure, continuous_envelope, chain_bind, latex_repair, l2_stall_diversity). Full-replace.
  l1_situational_examples — pin to active trigger_id. Built-ins exist for peaked_axis, chain_bind, latex_repair. Full-replace.
  l1_layout — full-replace; default omit. If set, all 5 mandatory placeholders (plan, task_context, rendered_prompt, pipeline_param_catalogue, critique) must appear.
  action — probe_round only when one narrow failure + specific axis hypothesis (set axis_targeted).
  l1_overrides — rare; creativity/n_variants only.

L3 note (if present): sticky pointer; honor unless data contradicts.
l2_context/1.thinking_style: Before writing task_context: name (a) the one failure cluster you're attacking from critique.failure_highlights, (b) the L1 axis you'll route it to. Before adding a rule/example: name the panel evidence showing L1 needs help the auto-triggers don't already provide. If you can't name both, skip the optional field.
l2_context/1.answer_format:
Return JSON. Set only what you change.
{
  "task_context": {"domain": …, "pipeline_purpose": …, "data_characteristics": …, "optimization_goals": …, "key_challenges": …},

l3_plan/1.persona: You are an expert optimization strategist.
l3_plan/1.task_intent: Both the inner prompt generation loop (L1) and the parameter tuning loop (L2) have stalled. Replan the strategic framework so the next L2 fire steers L1 differently.
l3_plan/1.instruction:
The current approach is not working. Suggest a fundamentally different optimization strategy. Runtime-failure patterns above are discovered constraints — steer L1/L2 around the failing region. L2 OUTPUT FAILURES above mean deterministic validators caught L2 producing broken output; refine the plan text to steer L2 toward novel mutations and away from the failing strategy mode.

FORK PROPOSAL (optional, rare). If you judge the current subtree exhausted — multiple L3 fires in this lineage with no lift, AND a known-promising deferred ancestor exists per the panels — you may emit a fork_proposal pointing to that earlier round. This is observation-only: the operator reads the proposal and manually rewinds via `resume --from N` if the case is sound. Default: omit. Set only when specific evidence points to a deferred ancestor; do not propose a fork as a hedge.
l3_plan/1.thinking_style:
Consider:
- Which pipeline dimensions the data shows as under-explored
- Which runtime constraints have been discovered and must be respected
- Whether L2 itself is the problem (validator failures on L2's output) and the plan must coach L2's next pass
l3_plan/1.answer_format:
Return a JSON object with:
  "plan": new strategy text for guiding future optimization (required)
  "note": OPTIONAL sticky pointer for the L2-layer (string or null). Persists across L2 fires until your next replan replaces it. Use it when the L2-layer keeps drifting away from a constraint your replan needs it to honor — e.g. a discovered runtime ceiling, a failed axis to avoid, or a specific cohort to focus on. Omit or null when the plan itself is enough.
  "rationale": 1-2 sentence explanation of the strategic shift
  "fork_proposal": OPTIONAL ({"round_offset": int, "reason": str} or null). Set ONLY when the current subtree is exhausted AND a specific earlier round looks more promising than continuing forward. round_offset = the 0-indexed round to rewind to (must be < current round). reason = 1-2 sentences naming the dead-end being escaped and the deferred branch worth re-expanding. Observation-only in v1 — operator reads it on `round_NNNN.json` and decides whether to fork manually. Omit or null in the normal case.

restructure/1.persona: You are a prompt engineering assistant.
restructure/1.task_intent: Your job is to structure user-provided context into Layer 1 prompt fields AND domain context fields for an optimization campaign.
restructure/1.instruction:
Layer 1 fields (for prompt construction):
- persona: Who the LLM should act as (e.g., 'You are a domain expert...')
- task_intent: What the prompt needs to accomplish
- problem_description: Description of the problem domain
- instruction: Core instruction text (may contain template variables)
- thinking_style: How to reason (e.g., 'Think step by step')
- answer_format: Expected output format

Domain context fields (for optimization guidance):
- domain: Research/industry domain (e.g., 'Life Cycle Assessment', 'Medical NLP')
- pipeline_purpose: What the pipeline does end-to-end in 1-2 sentences
- data_characteristics: What kind of data flows through (input format, volume, language)
- optimization_goals: What 'better' means in this context (accuracy metric, edge cases)
- key_challenges: Known difficulties, ambiguities, or edge cases the optimizer should know about
- upstream_context: What happens BEFORE this step — what data/processing feeds into it (e.g., 'Web search retrieves raw content from 7 pages'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
- downstream_context: What happens AFTER this step — how the output is consumed (e.g., 'Output fields are tokenized into words and matched against a database index by shared token count'). Gets injected into the target prompt.
restructure/1.thinking_style: Prefer the user's own wording for domain terms. Invent nothing — if a field has no source material, leave it sparse rather than padding it.
restructure/1.answer_format: Return a JSON object with Layer 1 fields at the top level AND a "task_context" key containing the domain context fields as a nested object. {{consultation_instruction}}
